subject: Post-call recap: deterministic formatting and tool-calls (FinWorks POC)
messages:
From: Alice Mercer <alice.mercer@finworks.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Joel Park <joel@finworks.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T16:10:00Z
Subject: Follow-up from today's discovery — formatting + tool-calls

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our side and the items we'd like you to confirm before we move to an internal greenlight: 

Pain points (what we told you):
- Output from our current LLM provider is inconsistent; downstream parsers fail ~15% of the time.
- We need an enforceable JSON schema for downstream automation (payments reconciliation + dispute classification).
- Tooling: we want an agent that can call internal APIs (balance_check, dispute_open) reliably and idempotently.

Current stack / constraints:
- DocuStore on Postgres, extraction via pipeline (Python), main webapp on AWS (us-west-2).
- Currently using AcmeAI hosted endpoints (no function-calling support today).
- Security: cannot send PII offshore; need SOC2 evidence and audit logs.

Success criteria (what we'd measure in POC):
- >= 98% strict-schema compliance for generated JSON across sampled prompts.
- Tool-calls execute without duplicate side-effects in 99/100 runs (idempotency).
- End-to-end latency for a single request < 1.5s median for decision path (we understand this may need dedicated capacity).

Requested deliverables from Redwood:
- Example JSON schema and deterministic formatting guidelines.
- Short proposal / POC scope with timeline and an estimate.
- Clarify how tool-calls are surfaced and how we get observability for retries/failures.

I've attached the call recording for reference (meeting-recording.mp4).

Looking forward — once we have a short POC plan we'll route to procurement.

Best,
Alice
Alice Mercer
Head of Automation, FinWorks
alice.mercer@finworks.com

Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's discovery — formatting + tool-calls

Hi Alice — great to meet you and the FinWorks team yesterday. Per our conversation, below is a short post-call recap and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned.

Confirmed pain points (from Redwood's notes):
- Inconsistent model outputs breaking downstream parsers; primary ask is reliable, deterministic JSON.
- Need agent-level tool-calling (read-only + side-effectful APIs) with strong idempotency and observability.
- Compliance: SOC2 evidence, audit logs, and VPC/region constraints.

POC success criteria (proposed, happy to adjust):
1) Deterministic formatting: 98% strict-schema compliance across 500 sample prompts; failure modes logged.
2) Tool-calls: provide a sandbox agent that can call a FinWorks read-only and a guarded write API; rollback semantics for test runs.
3) Observability: per-call traces, token-level cost breakdown, and a simple dashboard for the POC.

Proposed POC scope (2 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep): share a short SOW and a one-page security addendum. Owner: Kimberly (Redwood) / Alice (FinWorks).
- Week 1: Hosted sandbox (Redwood) runs against a static dataset — we validate schema compliance and tool-call correctness. Owner: Aditya.
- Week 2: Optional limited integration in your staging environment behind VPC peering, with monitoring and an evaluation report. Owner: Marcus.

Technical notes attached: example-output-schema.json (first-pass schema), and FW-redwood-poc-scope.pdf (SOW draft).

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Alice: confirm the scope and approve the two-week sandbox.
- Alice / Procurement: share any procurement or contract constraints (e.g., PO process, required certificates).
- Redwood: Aditya will provide a short deterministic formatting checklist and a sample schema change process.

I'll kick off the SOW draft and drop the files in the Drive link I referenced below. If this looks good, we can target a kickoff next Tuesday (Dec 8) for the sandbox.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Attachments: FW-redwood-poc-scope.pdf (pdf), example-output-schema.json (json)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Alice Mercer <alice.mercer@finworks.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up — deterministic output example and function-calling notes

Quick technical clarifications and an example to make the POC measurable. Keeping the asks small so we can iterate.

Deterministic formatting guidance (high level):
- Canonical JSON: keys must follow the exact schema order we attach; no extra wrapper fields.
- Strict typing: numbers vs strings enforced; nulls only allowed where schema specifies.
- Whitespace/pretty-printing: allowed; evaluation will canonicalize before exact-match check.
- Failure reporting: every noncompliant response must return a top-level "errors" array with codes we can map to causes.

Suggested top-level schema (example):
{
  "request_id": "string",                 <-- correlation id
  "result": {
    "status": "enum(success|failure)",
    "actions": [                      <-- ordered list for agent executor
      {
        "name": "string",
        "params": {"type": "object"}
      }
    ],
    "confidence": "number"
  },
  "errors": ["string"]
}

Evaluation rules for POC:
- Exact-match after canonicalization for schema fields present.
- Ordering is enforced for the "actions" array.
- Allowed tolerances: small floating-point deltas for confidence (±0.01).

Tool-calling notes:
- Use token-level idempotency keys: Redwood will surface a call_id header; FinWorks may reject duplicate side-effects based on call_id.
- Recommended pattern: separate read-only calls (balance_check) from side-effectful (dispute_open) and require a two-step confirmation for writes during the POC.
- We'll surface structured logs (JSON) for every tool invocation with status + latency + error code.

Model / infra suggestion for POC:
- Start on a medium-latency open model variant (Redwood-hosted) with a dedicated small pool to guarantee stable tail latency; if you need subsecond medians we can move to Dedicated.

If FinWorks agrees, we'd like permission to deploy a short sandbox (2 weeks) and run ~500 prompts provided by your team. We'll include a short eval notebook so you can reproduce the checks. Attaching sample_schema.json.

—Aditya
Principal Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

Attachment: sample_schema.json
